emails.subject: URGENT: Emergency Unblinding Request - Study DNL593-202, Subject 202-015-008
emails.body:
URGENT - EMERGENCY UNBLINDING REQUEST

Study: DNL593-202 (Part B)
Site: 015 - City Medical Center
Subject ID: 202-015-008

Dear DNL Clinical Team,

We are requesting emergency unblinding for the above subject who was admitted to our hospital approximately 2 hours ago following a generalized tonic-clonic seizure.

Patient Details:
- Female, 58 years old
- Randomized to Part B on 2024-01-10
- Currently on Day 65 of treatment
- No prior history of seizures

Current Status:
- Patient is stabilized but remains in the Emergency Department
- Neurology has been consulted
- The treating neurologist (Dr. Robert Kim) needs to know the treatment assignment to determine appropriate management, particularly regarding potential drug interactions and whether the seizure could be related to study drug

This is a serious adverse event and we believe emergency unblinding is medically necessary to guide appropriate treatment decisions.

Please advise on the process to proceed with emergency unblinding as soon as possible.

Thank you,

Sarah Chen, RN, CCRC
Clinical Research Coordinator
City Medical Center
Phone: (555) 234-5678
Pager: (555) 234-5679

emails.subject: RE: URGENT: Emergency Unblinding Request - Study DNL593-202, Subject 202-015-008
emails.body:
Dear Sarah and Dr. Martinez,

Thank you for this urgent notification. We take this matter very seriously and are mobilizing our team to address this emergency unblinding request.

I have copied:
- Dr. Patricia Reynolds (Medical Monitor)
- David Foster (Clinical Operations Director)
- Our unblinding team

To proceed with emergency unblinding, we need the following additional information:

1. Confirmation from the treating physician (Dr. Kim) that knowledge of treatment assignment is medically necessary for patient care
2. Brief description of seizure presentation and current clinical status
3. Current medications and recent changes
4. Any other relevant clinical information that supports the need for emergency unblinding
5. Contact information for Dr. Kim in case our Medical Monitor needs to discuss directly

Once we receive this information, Dr. Reynolds will review and approve the emergency unblinding if criteria are met. The unblinding can typically be completed within 1-2 hours of approval.

Please also confirm:
- Has the IRB been notified of this SAE?
- Has the SAE report been initiated?

We will expedite this process. Please call my cell at (555) 789-0123 if you need immediate assistance.

Best regards,

Jennifer Wong, PhD
Senior Clinical Trial Manager
DNL Pharmaceuticals
Cell: (555) 789-0123

emails.subject: RE: URGENT: Emergency Unblinding Request - Study DNL593-202, Subject 202-015-008
emails.body:
Dear Jennifer and DNL Team,

Thank you for the rapid response. I am providing the requested information below:

1. TREATING PHYSICIAN CONFIRMATION:
Dr. Robert Kim (Neurology) has confirmed that knowledge of treatment assignment is medically necessary. He needs to know whether the patient received DNL593 to:
   a) Assess if the seizure could be drug-related
   b) Determine if there are potential interactions with anti-seizure medications he is considering
   c) Guide monitoring and management decisions

Dr. Kim is available at (555) 234-5690 or r.kim@citymedicalcenter.org

2. SEIZURE PRESENTATION:
- Witnessed generalized tonic-clonic seizure at home, duration approximately 3 minutes
- Post-ictal confusion for approximately 20 minutes
- Patient called 911, transported to ED
- On arrival: Alert and oriented, vital signs stable
- No focal neurological deficits on examination
- Currently awaiting CT head and EEG

3. CURRENT MEDICATIONS:
- Study drug (DNL593 or placebo) - last dose this morning
- Lisinopril 10mg daily (unchanged for 2 years)
- Atorvastatin 20mg daily (unchanged for 1 year)
- Multivitamin daily
- No recent medication changes

4. ADDITIONAL RELEVANT INFORMATION:
- No prior seizure history
- No recent head trauma
- No fever or signs of infection
- No alcohol or illicit drug use
- Patient reports mild headache for past 2 days, otherwise no new symptoms
- All prior study visits showed no safety concerns
- Last lab work (Day 56) was within normal limits

5. IRB NOTIFICATION:
- IRB notification will be submitted today per our institution's policy
- SAE report is being prepared and will be submitted within 24 hours

Please expedite the unblinding process. The patient is stable but Dr. Kim would like to make treatment decisions as soon as possible.

Thank you,

Dr. Maria Martinez, MD
Principal Investigator
City Medical Center
Direct: (555) 234-5681

emails.subject: RE: URGENT: Emergency Unblinding Request - Study DNL593-202, Subject 202-015-008 - APPROVED
emails.body:
Dear Dr. Martinez and team,

Thank you for the comprehensive clinical information.

After reviewing the details provided, I am APPROVING this emergency unblinding request. The clinical justification is appropriate - knowledge of treatment assignment is medically necessary to guide the treating physician's management decisions for this serious adverse event.

I am directing our unblinding team to proceed immediately with the emergency unblinding process.

Unblinding team: Please provide the treatment assignment to Dr. Martinez and Dr. Kim within the next 30 minutes. Standard emergency unblinding procedures should be followed, including:
- Documentation of all individuals unblinded
- Confirmation of receipt
- Notification to appropriate regulatory personnel

Dr. Martinez: Please ensure that:
1. Only those individuals with a medical need to know are unblinded
2. Study drug is discontinued immediately (regardless of assignment)
3. The patient is followed per protocol SAE reporting requirements
4. We receive the completed SAE report within 24 hours

I am available if Dr. Kim would like to discuss any clinical concerns at (555) 345-6789.

Best regards,

Dr. Patricia Reynolds, MD, PhD
Medical Monitor
DNL Pharmaceuticals
Cell: (555) 345-6789

emails.subject: RE: CONFIDENTIAL: Emergency Unblinding Result - Study DNL593-202, Subject 202-015-008
emails.body:
Dear Michael and DNL Team,

I confirm receipt of the emergency unblinding information for subject 202-015-008.

TREATMENT ASSIGNMENT RECEIVED: PLACEBO

This information has been shared with:
1. Dr. Maria Martinez (Principal Investigator) - myself
2. Dr. Robert Kim (Treating Neurologist)
3. Sarah Chen (Clinical Research Coordinator) - for documentation purposes

Actions taken:
1. Study drug (placebo) discontinued - patient instructed not to take any further doses
2. Dr. Kim has been informed of the treatment assignment
3. Patient will continue to be managed per standard of care for new-onset seizure
4. All study drug supplies will be returned

Current patient status:
- CT head: Normal, no acute findings
- EEG: Scheduled for tomorrow
- Patient remains stable and will likely be admitted overnight for observation
- Neurology is proceeding with standard workup for first-time seizure

Next steps:
1. Complete SAE report - will submit within 24 hours
2. IRB notification - being submitted today
3. Patient will be withdrawn from study per protocol
4. Follow-up safety visit will be scheduled per protocol requirements

Thank you for the rapid response to this emergency situation.

Best regards,

Dr. Maria Martinez, MD
Principal Investigator
City Medical Center

emails.subject: RE: CONFIDENTIAL: Emergency Unblinding Result - Study DNL593-202, Subject 202-015-008 - Follow-up
emails.body:
Dear Dr. Martinez and Sarah,

Thank you for the confirmation and update on the patient's status. We are relieved to hear that the patient is stable.

A few follow-up items:

1. SAE REPORTING:
   - Please submit the initial SAE report within 24 hours as planned
   - We will need follow-up reports as new information becomes available
   - Please include all relevant medical records, imaging results, and EEG findings

2. STUDY DRUG:
   - Please complete the drug accountability records
   - All unused study drug should be returned or destroyed per protocol
   - Document the date of last dose in the eCRF

3. SUBJECT WITHDRAWAL:
   - Please complete the Early Termination eCRF pages
   - Reason: Withdrawal due to adverse event
   - Early termination visit should be scheduled per protocol (within 7 days if possible)

4. SAFETY FOLLOW-UP:
   - 30-day safety follow-up will be required per protocol
   - Please keep us updated on the patient's clinical course and final diagnosis

5. REGULATORY:
   - Our regulatory team will handle sponsor reporting requirements
   - Please provide IRB approval letter once received

Dr. Reynolds (Medical Monitor) may reach out with additional questions as she reviews the case.

Please don't hesitate to contact me if you need any assistance or have questions.

Wishing the patient a full recovery.

Best regards,

Jennifer Wong, PhD
Senior Clinical Trial Manager
DNL Pharmaceuticals

emails.subject: RE: CONFIDENTIAL: Emergency Unblinding Result - Study DNL593-202, Subject 202-015-008 - Patient Update
emails.body:
Dear Jennifer and DNL Team,

I wanted to provide an update on subject 202-015-008:

PATIENT STATUS (24 hours post-event):
- Patient was admitted overnight for observation
- EEG completed this morning - preliminary read shows no epileptiform activity
- No additional seizures
- Patient is neurologically intact
- Being discharged home today with neurology follow-up

NEUROLOGY ASSESSMENT:
Dr. Kim's impression is that this was likely a provoked seizure. Contributing factors being investigated:
- Sleep deprivation (patient reports poor sleep for past week)
- Possible viral prodrome (mild headache, fatigue)
- Patient will follow up with neurology in 2 weeks
- No anti-seizure medications prescribed at this time
- Driving restrictions per state law

STUDY DOCUMENTATION:
- Initial SAE report submitted to DNL portal at 09:00 today
- IRB notification submitted yesterday
- Drug accountability completed - all unused study drug quarantined for return
- Early termination visit scheduled for March 22, 2024

The patient and her family are grateful for the quick response and coordination between teams.

Please let me know if you need any additional information.

Best regards,

Sarah Chen, RN, CCRC
Clinical Research Coordinator
City Medical Center
